lead_headline: Restaurant pipeline crosses April 1 threshold at 77 leads (37 openings, 40 closures) as kosher newcomer L'Chaim opens Virginia Vale while foreclosure filings slip to 35—lowest weekly tally since late February

restaurant.blurb: 2 new leads today (1 opening, 1 closure) push total inventory to 77 leads (37 openings, 40 closures)—April 1 marks quarter's highest daily count. Fresh additions: L'Chaim Ma'adenei Melech opens Virginia Vale with Bukharian/Uzbek kosher cuisine (Katanov family operation, March media coverage); El Sotol Cocina Bar flags Westminster permanent closure at 4.5-star Dos Patrias location. March exits with 77-case surge—41% climb from February's 55-lead close—driven by Union Station opening density (8 active leads) and accelerating franchise closures (three Dairy Queen shutdowns, two California Pizza Kitchen flags). Lead quality holds: 88% score confidence 8+, signaling Claude verification rigor. Q1 pattern emerges: downtown corridor openings (Union Station, City Park) offset suburban fast-food retrenchment as kosher/specialty concepts fill neighborhood gaps.

foreclosure.blurb: 35 filings this week slide 17% below prior week's 42 to mark March's softest stretch since late February—top case caps at $686K Arapahoe property (24296 E Ohio Drive) with zero $2M+ outliers for first sub-million ceiling since mid-February; 136 auctions scheduled next 7 days.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today—April 1 quarterly deadline passes with no filings, extending March's 32-day statewide drought into uncharted territory. Previous record void capped at 12 days (December 2024 holiday window); sustained silence now confirms systemic database lag vs organic demand collapse. Archive context: 12,316 tracked cases show no comparable blackout. Critical inflection: if Wednesday delivers zero filings, escalate to state Liquor Enforcement Division for system status—expect 50-70 application backlog representing suppressed March/early April activity once database resumes. Social media chatter absent, suggesting applicant-side awareness of processing delays rather than regulatory freeze.

reputation.blurb: 11 mentions yesterday close March with 63 weekly citations (+26% vs prior week's 50)—sixth consecutive weekly gain as Instagram claims 29% share (18 pickups), Denver Post contributes 14%, x.com adds 10%. Top threads: Wash Park Social replacement coverage (Denver Post, Hoodline double-feature March 31); Castle Rock brewery widow story drives Hoodline pickup; Union Station Focus building neglect flags Post municipal desk. Platform diversification accelerates: social channels (Instagram, Facebook, x.com) now command 54% total vs legacy media's 24%—inverting Q1's 58%/42% historical split. Four-week rolling average settles at 57 mentions/week (+18% vs Q1 baseline), projecting 2,964 annual citations if April sustains March momentum. March exits as strongest month since tracking began—214 total mentions establish new benchmark.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) closes March at MTD +0 flat (+0.0/day)—April 1 reset comes as 90-day net holds +126. Tuesday's solo acquisition mirrors Monday's pattern, but March finishes underwater: final tally shows +21 new, −21 canceled across 31 days vs February's +58 net (+1.9/day). Recent deterioration sharpens: past 14 days post +12 net (22 new, 10 canceled, 0.9/day) vs prior two weeks' +30 net (41 new, 11 canceled, 2.1/day)—acquisition velocity drops 46% while churn climbs 27%. Longer arc: 90-day +126 still tracks 88% ahead of YTD's +1.4/day baseline, but March's zero-net close marks first monthly stall since November 2025. April opens with vulnerability: if current 0.9/day pace persists, Q2 risks first quarterly decline since tracking began. Watch for Wednesday retention signals.
